verification_steps.evidence: Reproduced via `TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d); export HOME=$TMPDIR; python3 todo.py add buy milk` — argparse emits `unrecognized arguments: milk` and exits 2; ~/.todo.json is NOT created. The literal contract step `Run: python todo.py add buy milk` fails.

Same root cause as vp-01: literal step `Run: python todo.py add fix tests` also fails with `unrecognized arguments: tests`. Internal auto-increment LOGIC works when invoked with quoted args (`add 'buy milk'` then `add 'fix tests'` produces ids [1,2]), but the contract-literal invocation form fails.

`python -m unittest discover -s tests` — 5/5 tests pass in 0.003s. Note: every test invokes `todo.main(["add", "buy milk"])` with the description pre-split into a single argv element; none exercise the shell-tokenised `add buy milk` path that the spec.md smoke check and contract literals require, so the test suite is vacuous against the actual bug.

drift_from_contract: done_looks_like[0]: `Running python todo.py add buy milk persists a new entry to ~/.todo.json with integer id=1, description='buy milk', ...` — the implementation defines the `description` positional as a single-token arg (no nargs='+' or equivalent), so the literal unquoted form `add buy milk` is rejected by argparse with `unrecognized arguments: milk` instead of persisting a `buy milk` task. The contract literal does not work.

findings.evidence: todo.py:82-85 — `add_parser.add_argument("description", help=...)` defines description as a single-token positional. Reproduced shell-side: `python3 todo.py add buy milk` -> `todo: error: unrecognized arguments: milk`, exit 2, ~/.todo.json not created. Spec.md S01 smoke check, contract C-S01-v2 done_looks_like[0], and vp-01 step `Run: python todo.py add buy milk` all use this literal unquoted multi-word form.
findings.gap: When the developer runs `todo add buy milk` (the literal in spec.md S01 smoke check and contract done_looks_like[0]), the CLI errors out instead of recording a task. Quoting the description (`todo add 'buy milk'`) works, but neither the spec smoke check nor the contract step nor any reasonable end-user workflow includes quotes. As written, the sprint does not deliver F01.
findings.suggested_fix_hint: Either declare description as `nargs='+'` and join with spaces in cmd_add, or accept the rest of the line via `nargs=argparse.REMAINDER`. The unit tests must then be augmented with a case that invokes `todo.main(['add', 'buy', 'milk'])` (multi-token argv) so this regression is caught next time.

findings.evidence: tests/test_add_task.py:34, 68, 117 — every add call uses `["add", "buy milk"]` (description pre-collapsed into one argv element). No test exercises `["add", "buy", "milk"]` or shell-tokenised invocation.
findings.gap: The unit-test suite is vacuous against the actual bug: it can only ever pass once description is already a single token, so it never catches the argparse misconfiguration that breaks the spec smoke literal. Tests demonstrate the internal helpers work; they do NOT demonstrate the CLI works as specified.
findings.suggested_fix_hint: Add a `test_add_multi_word_description` case that calls `todo.main(['add', 'buy', 'milk'])` and asserts the persisted entry has `description == 'buy milk'`. This is the test that, written first, would have made the implementer choose `nargs='+'`.

findings.evidence: todo.py:59 — `assert isinstance(next_id, int)`. Asserts are an internal-only check that disappears under `python -O`. Acceptable for now; flagged so it doesn't become a robustness regression if the schema ever evolves (e.g., gets a `archived` flag that someone might confuse for `id`).
findings.gap: Defensive assert against a self-controlled schema is dead weight; in a CLI run with `-O` the type narrowing it expresses disappears silently.
findings.suggested_fix_hint: Drop the assert; rely on the type annotation + mypy --strict for the narrowing.
